message.content:
**Answer:**  
One of the most celebrated sculptures of the 19th‑century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin**, completed in 1889. It became an icon of Romanticism and modern art, influencing countless artists and remaining a staple of museums worldwide.  

Other notable 19th‑century masterpieces include:

| Artist | Sculpture | Year |
|--------|-----------|------|
| Auguste Rodin | “The Gates of Hell” (series of works, 1880–1917) | 1880–1917 |
| Antonio Canova | “Psyche Revived by Cupid’s Kiss” (original 1787, but its influence persisted into the 19th century) | 1787 |
| Jean-Baptiste Léonard | “La Marseillaise” (statue of Marianne) | 1835 |
| Hiram Owen | “The Spirit of the Republic” (Statue of Liberty) | 1886 |

These works illustrate the range of styles—from neoclassicism to romantic realism—that defined 19th‑century sculpture.
